A0062.title: Video Surveillance
A0062.definition: A technology that uses cameras, monitors, computer software and hardware, and other technical means to perform real-time monitoring and remote control of specific areas.
A0062.description: Traditional surveillance systems consist of front-end cameras, transmission cables, and a video monitoring platform. Cameras can be divided into network digital cameras and analog cameras, serving as the front-end devices for video image signal acquisition. Video surveillance is widely used in many scenarios due to its intuitiveness, accuracy, timeliness, and rich information content. Modern surveillance systems can utilize smartphones, while also performing automatic image recognition, storage, and automatic alarms. Video data is transmitted back to the control host via 3G/4G/WIFI, and the host can perform real-time viewing, recording, playback, retrieval, and storage operations, thereby enabling mobile-connected video surveillance.
A0062.limitation: Video surveillance heavily relies on human recognition of images, which has a certain lag and is prone to fatigue-related missed detections. Attackers can bypass recognition by using disguises, obstructions, or operating at night. Changes in lighting and normal pedestrian movement can easily generate false alarm noise.
